connectionSpecification.description: Reads tables and views of a Microsoft SQL Server database: full refresh, or incremental by a cursor column.

authentication.description: SQL: a SQL Server login. NTLM: a Windows domain account (username DOMAIN\user), for a server joined to a Windows domain.
authentication.title: Authentication

password.description: The password associated with the username.
password.title: Password

schemas.description: The list of schemas to sync from.
schemas.title: Schemas

ssl_method.description: The encryption method which is used when communicating with the database.

oneOf.description: Data transfer will not be encrypted; only the login is, when the server supports encryption.
oneOf.title: Unencrypted

oneOf.description: Use the certificate provided by the server without verification. (For testing purposes only!)
oneOf.title: Encrypted (trust server certificate)

oneOf.description: Verify and use the certificate provided by the server.

certificate.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the server certificate. Empty: the CAs trusted by the connector image.
certificate.title: CA Certificate

hostNameInCertificate.description: The host name the server certificate must name. Empty: the configured host. Set it when the connector reaches the server by another name, such as an IP address.
hostNameInCertificate.title: Host Name In Certificate

oneOf.title: Encrypted (verify certificate)

ssl_method.title: SSL Method

tunnel_method.description: Whether to initiate an SSH tunnel before connecting to the database, and if so, which kind of authentication to use.
No ssh tunnel needed to connect to database

ssh_key.description: OS-level user account ssh key credentials in PEM or OpenSSH format (RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519)
ssh_key.title: SSH Private Key

tunnel_host.description: Hostname of the jump server host that allows inbound ssh tunnel.
tunnel_host.title: SSH Tunnel Jump Server Host

tunnel_host_key.description: Public host keys of the jump server, one per line, each in authorized_keys format ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA...") or as a known_hosts line ("bastion.example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."); the whole output of ssh-keyscan works. The tunnel is refused when the server presents none of them. When empty, the host key is not verified.
tunnel_host_key.title: SSH Host Key

tunnel_method.description: Connect through a jump server tunnel host using username and ssh key

tunnel_port.description: Port on the proxy/jump server that accepts inbound ssh connections.
tunnel_port.title: SSH Connection Port

tunnel_user.description: OS-level username for logging into the jump server host.
tunnel_user.title: SSH Login Username

tunnel_host.description: Hostname of the jump server host that allows inbound ssh tunnel.
tunnel_host.title: SSH Tunnel Jump Server Host

tunnel_host_key.description: Public host keys of the jump server, one per line, each in authorized_keys format ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA...") or as a known_hosts line ("bastion.example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."); the whole output of ssh-keyscan works. The tunnel is refused when the server presents none of them. When empty, the host key is not verified.
tunnel_host_key.title: SSH Host Key

tunnel_method.description: Connect through a jump server tunnel host using username and password authentication

tunnel_port.title: SSH Connection Port

tunnel_user.description: OS-level username for logging into the jump server host.
tunnel_user.title: SSH Login Username

tunnel_user_password.description: OS-level password for logging into the jump server host
tunnel_user_password.title: Password

tunnel_method.title: SSH Tunnel Method

username.description: The username which is used to access the database. With NTLM authentication, the Windows account as DOMAIN\user.
username.title: Username
